statement: Prove that the composition of two continuous functions is continuous.
solution: Let f:X→Y, g:Y→Z be continuous and W⊆Z open. Then g^{-1}(W) is open in Y (g continuous), so f^{-1}(g^{-1}(W))=(g∘f)^{-1}(W) is open in X (f continuous). Hence g∘f is continuous.

statement: Prove that every constant function between topological spaces is continuous.
solution: Let f(x)=y0 for all x. For open V⊆Y, f^{-1}(V)=X if y0∈V and ∅ otherwise; both are open. So f is continuous.

statement: Prove that the inclusion map of a subspace A into X is continuous.
solution: Let i:A→X be inclusion. For U open in X, i^{-1}(U)=A∩U, which is open in the subspace topology on A by definition. Hence i is continuous.

statement: Prove that the restriction of a continuous function to a subspace is continuous.
solution: If f:X→Y is continuous and A⊆X, then f|A = f∘i where i:A→X is the (continuous) inclusion. A composition of continuous maps is continuous (c01), so f|A is continuous.

statement: Prove that f: X → Y is continuous if and only if for every x and every neighborhood V of f(x) there is a neighborhood U of x with f(U) ⊆ V.
solution: (⇒) Given V open ∋ f(x), U=f^{-1}(V) is open, contains x, and f(U)⊆V. (⇐) Let V open; for each x∈f^{-1}(V) get U_x with f(U_x)⊆V so U_x⊆f^{-1}(V). Then f^{-1}(V)=∪U_x is open.

statement: State and prove the pasting lemma for two closed sets.
solution: Let X=A∪B with A,B closed, and f:A→Y, g:B→Y continuous agreeing on A∩B. Define h=f on A, g on B. For closed C⊆Y, h^{-1}(C)=f^{-1}(C)∪g^{-1}(C); f^{-1}(C) is closed in A hence in X (A closed), likewise g^{-1}(C), so h^{-1}(C) is closed. Thus h is continuous.

statement: Prove that a map f: Z → X × Y into a product is continuous if and only if both component maps π_X ∘ f and π_Y ∘ f are continuous.
solution: (⇒) Projections are continuous and compositions of continuous maps are continuous. (⇐) The product topology has subbasis {π_X^{-1}(U), π_Y^{-1}(V)}. Preimages under f are (π_X∘f)^{-1}(U) and (π_Y∘f)^{-1}(V), open by hypothesis. A map with open preimages of subbasis elements is continuous.

statement: Prove that the projection map π_X: X × Y → X is an open map.
solution: Basic open sets of X×Y are U×V with U,V open. π_X(U×V)=U (when V≠∅), which is open. An arbitrary open set is a union of such boxes, and π_X of a union is the union of images, hence open. So π_X maps open sets to open sets.

statement: Prove that being homeomorphic is an equivalence relation on topological spaces.
solution: Reflexive: the identity is a homeomorphism. Symmetric: if f is a homeomorphism so is f^{-1} (bijective, and both it and its inverse f are continuous). Transitive: a composition of homeomorphisms is a homeomorphism (bijective, and compositions of continuous maps are continuous, c01).

statement: Prove that a continuous bijection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism.
solution: Let f:X→Y be a continuous bijection, X compact, Y Hausdorff. To show f^{-1} continuous, show f is closed: if C⊆X is closed then C is compact (closed in compact), f(C) is compact (continuous image), and compact subsets of Hausdorff spaces are closed. So f maps closed sets to closed sets, i.e. f^{-1} is continuous.

statement: Prove that the map x ↦ (x, f(x)) from X to X × Y is continuous if and only if f: X → Y is continuous.
solution: Call the map g. Its components are the identity on X (always continuous) and f. By c07 g is continuous iff both components are, i.e. iff f is continuous.

statement: Prove that f: X → Y is continuous if and only if f(cl(A)) ⊆ cl(f(A)) for every A ⊆ X.
solution: (⇒) cl(f(A)) is closed, so f^{-1}(cl(f(A))) is closed and contains A, hence contains cl(A); thus f(cl(A))⊆cl(f(A)). (⇐) Let C⊆Y closed, A=f^{-1}(C). Then f(cl(A))⊆cl(f(A))⊆cl(C)=C, so cl(A)⊆f^{-1}(C)=A, making A closed. Closed preimages of closed sets give continuity.

statement: Let q: X → Y be a quotient map. Prove that a map g: Y → Z is continuous if and only if g ∘ q is continuous.
solution: (⇒) Composition of continuous maps. (⇐) Let V⊆Z open. Then (g∘q)^{-1}(V)=q^{-1}(g^{-1}(V)) is open in X. Since q is a quotient map, a set W⊆Y is open iff q^{-1}(W) is open; taking W=g^{-1}(V) shows g^{-1}(V) is open. Hence g is continuous.

statement: Prove that if f: X → Y is a homeomorphism then X is compact if and only if Y is compact.
solution: If X is compact, then Y=f(X) is the continuous image of a compact space, hence compact. Applying the same to the homeomorphism f^{-1} gives the converse. So compactness is preserved by homeomorphism.

statement: Prove that two continuous maps f, g: X → Y into a Hausdorff space that agree on a dense subset D are equal.
solution: Consider E={x: f(x)=g(x)}. Since Y is Hausdorff, E is closed (it is the preimage of the diagonal, which is closed in Y×Y, under the continuous map x↦(f(x),g(x))). E⊇D and D is dense, so E⊇cl(D)=X. Hence f=g.

statement: Prove that if f: X → Y is continuous and Y is Hausdorff, then the graph of f is closed in X × Y.
solution: The graph is G={(x,y):y=f(x)}. The map h(x,y)=(f(x),y) is continuous into Y×Y, and G=h^{-1}(Δ) where Δ is the diagonal. Since Y is Hausdorff, Δ is closed in Y×Y, so G is closed.

statement: Prove that a function into a discrete space is continuous if and only if it is locally constant.
solution: In a discrete codomain every singleton {y} is open, so f^{-1}({y}) is open for continuous f; these open fibers partition X, so f is constant on a neighborhood of each point (locally constant). Conversely if f is locally constant, each f^{-1}({y}) is a union of the neighborhoods on which f=y, hence open, and every subset of the codomain is a union of singletons, so all preimages are open.

statement: Prove that a bijective continuous open map is a homeomorphism.
solution: Let f be a continuous open bijection. Open-ness means f maps open sets to open sets; equivalently, for every open U, (f^{-1})^{-1}(U)=f(U) is open, so f^{-1} is continuous. With f continuous and bijective, f is a homeomorphism.

statement: Prove transitivity of the subspace topology: if A ⊆ B ⊆ X, the subspace topology A inherits from B equals the one it inherits from X.
solution: Open sets of B are B∩U for U open in X; intersecting with A gives A∩(B∩U)=A∩U since A⊆B. So sets open in A-from-B are exactly A∩U for U open in X, which is the A-from-X subspace topology.

statement: Prove that the product X × Y is homeomorphic to Y × X.
solution: The swap map s(x,y)=(y,x) is a bijection. Its components are the projections, which are continuous, so s is continuous (c07); likewise its inverse (the swap the other way) is continuous. Hence s is a homeomorphism.
